If you have friends to play with and enjoy a good bit of coop then grab this game up and have a blast turning Xenomorphs into green sizzling soup. After playing every Aliens game in the past 20 years this is the high point. The classes, while nothing groundbreaking, are fun to play. The Perk system is very well done, with perks being able to be built onto each other and even some perks from other classes being able to be included. This means that for some of the best builds you HAVE to play other classes a bit to unlock those perks. To some this may be a downside, But I think its great. It gets you out of the classes you are comfortable with and teaches you a lot about them and their limitations as you level them up. 

The major downside so far for me is the lack of maps. There are only 4 overall missions that are broken down into 3 maps each. This IS saved to a degree by the difficulty being able to be ramped up considerably and a card system that has a nice bonus vs reward scheme that is very well done and creatively thematic. 

I have loved my time with it and had some great fun with a few friends leveling the classes up. The devs have already listened to a lot of comments and made changes, adding new classes and modes, along with tons of new weapons and attachments, they are showing that they are committed to the game fpr a while yet to come. 
So if you want a good coop game that does some real justice to its source material, then jump on this one and ROCK!

This game hits the bullseye in terms of a third-person shooter done right. With high replay value and endless hordes of bloodthirsty aliens to blast away to your heart's content, this game offers roughly 100 or so hours of enjoyment before it begins to feel redundant. With multiple classes, weapons, abilities, and gadgets at your disposal, you and your fireteam are a force to be reckoned with and you FEEL it. But, however, the aliens are no pushovers either; step it up a notch by playing on higher difficulties, and you'll be hard pressed to make it to the end of a level with you and your fireteam intact. Successfully completing these harder missions requires solid preparations beforehand as well as selfless teamwork and communication. This brings me to my biggest complaint about the game: there is absolutely no form of in game communication, no vc and no text. You must either look for teammates in their Discord, already have friends with the game, or chance that the randos you play with won't be completely selfish garbage (good luck). All in all, the story line is readily bland and quickly forgotten, but hey that's not what you're playing this for, this is a game about blasting ugly aliens to kingdom come and then trying not to smash your keyboard when you get clapped by the absolute very last alien in the level after spending 30 minutes of your life trying beat the mission on a harder setting. Additionally, the challenge card system (various mission mods) puts an exciting spin on traditional game play: want to torture yourself by turning every fodder enemy into heavy class prowler? No problem we got you! Or perhaps you want to give yourself an edge by playing a card that multiplies your mag size and ammo reserves? We got you! Still can't get enough blood and violence? Play horde mode after finishing the main campaign and battle endless waves of increasingly difficult enemies for even more rewards. The AI teammates in the game are only useful at lower difficulties, but they're still better than many of the randos you'll get matched with.

To summarize, I highly recommend! You shoot aliens. You have fun. You die by boss alien. You sad. You retry with better strategy. You kill all aliens. You happy. You have fun.
